title: Alert Bloom Mitigator and Runbook Simulation Bench
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: During region flaps and partial capacity losses we see 'alert blooms' — a transient spike of low-signal alerts that overwhelm on-call and mask real SLO degradations. Current suppression rules are static and tuned per-metric, leading to either noisy pages or delayed detection. Goal: build an adaptive mitigator that combines fractional pager sampling, short-window statistical bloom detection, and coordinated circuit-breaker-driven load-shedding + automated runbook activation. Also deliver a runbook simulation bench so SREs can rehearse incidents and validate suppression policies before rollout.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic bloom-detection algorithm implemented in the alert pipeline that flags >90% of historical bloom events while keeping false-suppression <5%
Pager-sampling feature that routes sampled pages to a shadow rota for visibility without waking primary on-call
Runbook simulation bench that can replay past telemetry (latency, error-rate, token-throttle) and emulate region failover to validate mitigation behavior
Automated circuit-breaker triggers that initiate controlled shedding policy and create a dedicated incident channel with runbook steps pre-populated
End-to-end tests and a staged rollout plan with telemetry dashboards and rollback criteria documented
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Kumar: Created ticket after postmortem for 2026-02-24 downtime. Initial scope includes detection heuristic, pager sampling, runbook automation, simulation bench. Linked to customer complaints about masked errors in multi-region failover.

2026-03-03 - Ethan Park: Spiked a prototype for bloom detector using median absolute deviation windowing and exponential smoothing. Early results: detects blooms within 30s in synthetic tests but misses very-low-amplitude coordinated spikes. Raising estimate to 8 points to add a second detector (correlation-driven).

2026-03-05 - Marta Ruiz (Design): Reviewed pager UX. Recommendation: when sampled pages are enabled, include a compact context banner and 'replay ID' to feed into the simulation bench. Also suggested a non-intrusive mobile badge for shadow rota members.
2026-03-07 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/alerting/pull/324 - implements bloom detector stage and sampling flag. Requesting review from infra-team and oncall-sre.
2026-03-08 - Security review note: no sensitive data in sampled pages; ensure sampling rate config is RBAC-protected. Emailed SecOps for signoff.

2026-03-10 - Integration test: runbook bench replayed the 2026-02-24 signal with region failover and confirmed the circuit-breaker triggered at the configured SLO breach window. Observed unexpected behavior: cache-priming KV-eviction caused a second wave of alerts after mitigation. Action: add a pre-shedding step to mark long-lived KV sessions and throttle priming aggressiveness.
2026-03-11 - Liam O'Neil (PM): Approved staging rollout plan. Staging targets: staging1 and canary region in us-west-2. Monitoring: per-route pager rate, false-suppression rate, time-to-detect.
implementation_notes: Detector composition: fast-window MAD detector + slower correlation detector across related metrics (latency, 5xx, token-rejects)
Pager-sampling: probabilistic sampling with deterministic hashing per-request to preserve duplicates; shadow rota receives full context with replay ID
Circuit-breaker: state machine with CLOSED -> PROBING -> OPEN; PROBING issues controlled low-rate traffic; OPEN triggers priority-0 shedding policy and automated incident creation
Runbook bench: accepts replay ID and can spin up synthetic canary loads, toggled KV eviction, and controlled region cutover using staging infra
Metrics to add: bloom_ratio (alerts per minute normalized by expected baseline), sampled_page_ratio, suppression_false_positive_rate, time_to_mitigate
